question_text: Consider two 1.0 L acetic-acid/sodium-acetate buffers under the textbook buffer model. One contains 1.0 M of each component; the other contains 0.10 M of each. Without calculating a numerical pH, compare their initial pH and buffer capacity and explain the reason for each comparison. Describe how the conjugate pair responds to a small addition of strong acid and, separately, to a small addition of strong base. Does buffering mean that either solution keeps its pH unchanged for arbitrarily large additions?
